rule: Every new parameter added to chart/values.yaml must also be declared in chart/values.schema.json
trigger: A key is added to values.yaml but no corresponding entry appears in values.schema.json
rationale: values.schema.json is both the authoritative documentation source and the Helm validation gate; omitting new parameters silently bypasses both

evidence.excerpt: it is a source for some documentation and also allows for values.yaml validations

rule: In the Airflow Helm chart, a component feature sub-flag (e.g. metricsEnabled, tracesEnabled) must be gated on its parent enabled flag so that Airflow is never pointed at a Service that does not exist
trigger: A template sets otel_on or otel_host from a sub-flag (e.g. .Values.otelCollector.metricsEnabled) without also checking .Values.otelCollector.enabled
rationale: metricsEnabled/tracesEnabled without otelCollector.enabled causes Airflow to send telemetry to a collector Service/Deployment that was never created

evidence.excerpt: can turn on OTel even when .Values.otelCollector.enabled is false, pointing Airflow to a collector that won't exist

rule: Hardcoded monitoring/telemetry parameters in Airflow Helm chart templates must be exposed as configurable values in values.yaml
trigger: A chart template or values.yaml hardcodes a monitoring interval or export period (e.g. OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_INTERVAL: "30000") without a corresponding values.yaml key
rationale: Monitoring resolution depends heavily on user requirements; hardcoding it removes the ability to tune without patching the chart

evidence.excerpt: Could we make it configurable? it will depend heavily on the user requirements regarding the monitoring resolution

rule: Do not duplicate a default value in a values.schema.json description string when the schema already encodes it via a default field
trigger: A description string in values.schema.json ends with 'Defaults to <X>.' where <X> is also specified in a sibling default field
rationale: Duplicating the default in prose creates a maintenance hazard when the default changes; the schema default field is authoritative

evidence.excerpt: suggestion removes the trailing 'Defaults to `connection`.' from the description

rule: When chart topology renames a component-scoped value path (e.g. ingress.enabled → ingress.apiServer.enabled), update existing Helm tests to use the new path instead of deleting them
trigger: A Helm test that previously used a broad values path (e.g. ingress.enabled) is deleted when the chart introduces a component-scoped path (e.g. ingress.apiServer.enabled)
rationale: Deleting the test instead of adapting it removes coverage of the component-level toggle; the test should be modified to target the new key

evidence.excerpt: we should modify this test case … instead of deleting it

rule: Release documentation for apache-airflow-mypy must use apache_airflow_mypy-... (underscore) filenames in twine upload commands, not apache_airflow.mypy-... (dot)
trigger: A twine upload command in release docs references a glob or filename with the pattern apache_airflow.mypy- (dot before mypy)
rationale: The distribution name apache-airflow-mypy produces wheel/sdist files named with underscores (apache_airflow_mypy-...); using a dot causes the upload glob to match nothing

evidence.excerpt: distribution name apache-airflow-mypy will produce files like apache_airflow_mypy-... (underscore)

rule: mypy configuration examples for apache-airflow-mypy must reference the airflow_mypy.plugins.* namespace, not airflow.mypy.plugins.*
trigger: A mypy plugins= line in documentation or configuration examples reads airflow.mypy.plugins.
rationale: After pip install apache-airflow-mypy the importable namespace is airflow_mypy.plugins.*; using airflow.mypy.plugins.* silently fails to load the plugins

evidence.excerpt: modules are airflow_mypy.plugins.* as also configured in the repo's pyproject.toml

rule: In Breeze's global_constants.py, DEFAULT_POSTGRES_VERSION must point to the oldest entry in the supported versions list so that PR CI catches accidental use of newer Postgres features
trigger: DEFAULT_POSTGRES_VERSION is set to the newest (e.g. [-1]) rather than the oldest ([0]) entry in CURRENT_POSTGRES_VERSIONS or ALLOWED_POSTGRES_VERSIONS
rationale: Most PRs run only the default version; using the oldest guarantees that features unavailable on older Postgres versions are caught at PR time, not in canary builds

evidence.excerpt: we always tested against the oldest version … risk we use cool new features and miss testing against an old version

rule: When building providers with flit_core via run_command, pass os.environ.copy() merged with SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH rather than a dict containing only SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH
trigger: A run_command call for a flit_core provider build sets env= to a dict with only SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH instead of {**os.environ, 'SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH': ...}
rationale: Passing only SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH strips PATH and other variables that flit requires to locate Python and its own dependencies, potentially breaking the build silently

evidence.excerpt: flit_core env is set to only SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH (wiping all other env vars) … may break if flit needs PATH

rule: In Breeze's path_utils.py, a gitdir: path parsed from a .git file must be resolved to an absolute path before use as a Docker bind-mount source
trigger: Code reads a gitdir: value from a .git file and constructs a Path from it without calling .resolve() or anchoring it to AIRFLOW_ROOT_PATH
rationale: A relative gitdir: value would be interpreted relative to cwd when passed to Docker as a bind-mount source, silently mounting the wrong directory or causing a Docker error

evidence.excerpt: relative path used as Docker bind-mount source would be interpreted relative to cwd, not AIRFLOW_ROOT_PATH
